title: Sunny and the Stick Insect | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka almost walks right past a stick insect clinging motionless to a moonlit branch — and when she finally sees it, she cannot believe how perfectly it has learned to look like nothing at all. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny almost walked past it.

She had been looking at the branch — really looking at it — when she noticed that one section of it was slightly different from the rest. Not different in colour. Not different in texture, really. Just slightly different in the way it sat.

She leaned closer.

The branch moved.

Not the branch. The stick insect. Clinging there so still, so perfectly twig-shaped, that her eyes had simply sorted it into the category of branch and moved on.

She stopped.

The stick insect had six legs, each one as thin as a thread. Its body was long and smooth and exactly the same pale brown as the branch it clung to. Even its antennae looked like twigs. Even the way it held its front legs extended forward — that was camouflage too, she realised. Making itself look longer. More like a twig.

It did not move.

She did not move.

They stayed like that — Sunny watching the stick insect, the stick insect being so still that it was almost not there at all.

She thought: it knows exactly how to rest. It has learned to be so calm that the whole world just... passes by.

She sat down quietly under the branch.

Maybe she could learn that too.

Be so still the world goes quiet.

The stick insect clung to its branch. Sunny leaned against the tree. And together they were still.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, stick insect. Goodnight, little one.
